fields: Encrypted single-use invitation delivery payload; cleared after delivery or failure; pending capabilities expire after seven days.
Authenticated wrapped tenant/environment data encryption keys, key versions and bounded resumable rotation state. Plaintext DEKs exist only in memory.
Tenant/environment customer key ARNs, binding lifecycle and encrypted write-only KMS grant tokens; authenticated customer-wrapped DEKs contain no applicant plaintext.
Immutable tenant/environment storage bucket routing and approved residency metadata; retained versions support deletion and restore.
activities.purpose: Authenticate users, administer tenants, enforce access, and investigate security events.
activities.retention: Account and membership lifetime, followed by the configured legal/security deletion period; short-lived tokens expire and are purged.
processors: Customer-approved AWS KMS, including CloudHSM-backed customer keys
activities.transfers: Tenant notification contact data is sent to the tenant-configured provider. Platform administrator invitation contact data and encrypted single-use delivery payload use deployment email configuration, never tenant provider credentials; terminal delivery clears the credential. The deployment owner records region and safeguards. Only random DEKs and connection probes are sent to the customer-approved KMS region; applicant plaintext stays in the application. Deployment records document region and safeguards.

activities.purpose: Create and execute tenant-requested identity verification workflows.
activities.retention: Tenant policy controls the verification record; session credentials are short-lived; minimization and deletion jobs apply after the case retention window.
activities.transfers: Only policy-required attributes/evidence are sent through enabled provider adapters; cross-border region and safeguards are deployment records.

activities.purpose: Assess document authenticity, extract asserted identity data, and produce biometric match/liveness evidence.
activities.retention: Uploads begin in temporary storage, move to protected media/evidence storage when consumed, and are deleted by tenant policy; derived biometric data follows the shortest applicable media/biometric period.
activities.transfers: Media leaves the deployment only when the tenant policy selects an external provider; provider region, subprocessors, and transfer mechanism must be recorded before enablement.

fields: Request provenance distinguishing direct immediate-peer metadata from signed portal context, ingress-asserted or unavailable subject IP, and browser-reported User-Agent
Versioned audit integrity hashes and authentication tags with nonsecret application key identifiers; no cryptographic key material is persisted in audit events.
activities.purpose: Demonstrate authorization, accountability, integrity, and compliance decisions.
activities.retention: Immutable consent/audit evidence follows contractual and statutory schedules; access is restricted and deletion is documented where legally permitted.
activities.transfers: Exports are disclosed only to authorized tenant users, auditors, regulators, or incident responders using approved secure channels.

fields: API client identity and secret hash
Unrated, production-only per-provider-check usage facts (tenant, project, outcome, capability, provider ownership, timestamps); no payments or prices.

Commercial plan prices and capability rates in integer currency subunits, tenant subscription, immutable monthly invoice snapshots, payment transaction references, signed callback digests and refund statuses (no card data).

Billing contact email sent to the selected hosted checkout provider; opaque checkout/session/payment transaction and event identifiers, checkout capability URLs, verified refund amounts and statuses, and dispute identifiers and outcomes. No card number, security code or bank credentials are collected or persisted by IdentityCore.
Subscription invoice attempt timestamps for fair, bounded retry scheduling
Usage reconciliation exception pointers, controlled error codes and failure timestamps
activities.purpose: Operate customer integrations, provider routing, metering, delivery troubleshooting, and support. Operate opt-in monthly billing, server-verified payment settlement, disputes and refunds.
activities.retention: Credential material lasts until rotation/revocation; delivery and support metadata follows operational/contractual schedules; ticket attachments must not contain verification media unless explicitly approved. Unrated usage facts require a tenant-approved contractual retention period, access controls and deletion/offboarding schedule before commercial activation. Billing records and gateway settlement references require an approved jurisdiction-specific accounting/tax retention and access policy; raw gateway webhooks and card data are not persisted.
processors: Paystack merchant account, when explicitly enabled
activities.transfers: Webhook payloads and support/provider disclosures follow tenant configuration and recorded destination safeguards. Paystack merchant API requests transmit billing email, GHS invoice amounts and opaque payment references. Card and bank account credentials remain solely with Paystack. Merchant eligibility, processing regions, retention and processor contracts require deployment-specific privacy approval.

fields: Environment-scoped review queue configuration, reviewer skills and availability, frozen priorities and SLA deadlines, and fair assignment timestamps.
Independent quality sampling percentage, frozen original decision and revision, maker/checker exclusions, reviewer assignments, encrypted assessment notes and disagreement outcomes.

Immutable SHA-256 digest of the original workflow template instantiation request, retained with its tenant-scoped replay key for the workflow configuration lifetime. The digest is a correlation value, not anonymized product telemetry.
activities.purpose: Configure tenant/environment-owned verification purposes, policies, catalogs and workflows; operate authorized processing and delivery.
activities.retention: Configuration lifetime and configured audit/security schedule; evidence and subject payloads in JSON containers follow their snapshotted purpose/environment retention and verified deletion controls.
activities.transfers: Repository configuration stays in the controlled application/database environment. Notifications and provider-selected processing require deployment-specific approved regions and processor contracts.

fields: client minute and organization minute/month aggregate counters
activities.purpose: Enforce atomic tenant/environment API quotas and display organization-only capacity and denial telemetry without request or evidence payloads.
activities.retention: Expired admitted/denied window counters are purged after 90 days by the retention worker. Quota configuration remains for the organization/environment lifetime.
activities.transfers: Counters remain in the controlled database and authenticated organization dashboard; no subjects, requests, secrets or evidence are sent to external processors.

fields: provider evidence envelopes and encrypted raw output
activities.purpose: Select declared providers for an authorized tenant/environment capability, test and independently approve credentials, and preserve auditable versioned verification evidence.
activities.retention: Active configuration and approval versions follow the controlled organization configuration schedule; obsolete encrypted credentials must be retired and purged under deployment credential-retention controls. Provider-check evidence follows verification policy metadata/media retention, verified subject deletion, and legal holds. Vendor retention is declared per manifest and checked against the deployment processor register.
activities.transfers: Credentials use only the encrypted application store and authorized HTTPS endpoint headers. Document evidence references and minimal derived risk signals flow only to declared providers for the assigned environment. Manifest regions, retention and transfer notes must match approved controller/vendor agreements.
